spans.s: utittira, onomat., a sound said to be uttered exceptionally by a tittira bird; see MSV 〔i.118.10〕; 〔120.18〕. (Tib. says only a different sound.)

uttima, adj. (= Pkt. id., Sheth, and Pischel 〔101〕; in AMg. uttimaṅga = uttamāṅga, Pischel l. c.; Skt. and Pali uttama; see 〔§ 22.16〕), highest, supreme: Mv 〔iii.268.1〕 ˚ma-yasaṃ, mss. (Senart em. uttama-yaśaṃ).
Uttiya, n. of a śreṣṭhin: Mv 〔i.36.3 ff.〕
uttiṣṭhate (special use of Skt. sthā plus ud, q.v. in BR s.v. 3), arises = is being built, of a house: Divy 〔304.12〕 (anyatarasya gṛhapater gṛham) ˚te.
ūti, f., effort (cf. BR s.v. 7: cited once from BhāgP.; no other mg. seems possible in Divy): Divy 〔654.27〕; 〔655.2〕 utsāhany ūtir aprativāṇiḥ … yogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ.
